card.name: Chacarera
card.era: Documented from early 20th century (Chazarreta scores, 1910s-1920s); claimed older rural roots
card.tagline: Lively Santiago del Estero couple dance with stomping and clapping.
card.profile: The chacarera is a fast, festive couples folk dance from Santiago del Estero, the rural counterpart to cosmopolitan tango. Dancers face each other without touching; men circle the women with foot-stomping (zapateo) and finger-snapping (castañetas) while women perform the swirling zarandeo, ending with the 'coronación' embrace. It is accompanied by guitar, violin, bombo legüero, and voice, sung in coplas; chacarera simple and doble are the main variants (English Wikipedia; Carnegie Hall).
card.insight: Standardized by Andrés Chazarreta's early-20th-century scores and the 1950s recordings of Los Hermanos Ábalos, the chacarera became a nationwide emblem of Argentine nativism and rural identity (English Wikipedia).
